message.content:
**Answer**

The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) was a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the early Paleocene. It belonged to the clade that eventually split into the two major lineages that give rise to the orders **Carnivora** (lion) and **Perissodactyla** (zebra). This ancestor would have had a generalized body plan—small, agile, with a flexible diet—typical of many early placental mammals that later diversified into the distinct lineages we see today.
